title: Disney+ and ESPN are testing AI-powered search that lets users describe what they want in plain language
excerpt: Disney+ and ESPN are beta testing AI search. ESPN answers sports questions from decades of data. Disney+ recommends shows based on mood, not just viewing history.
content_html:
TL;DR

Disney+ and ESPN are beta testing AI search with small user groups. ESPN answers natural language sports queries. Disney+ recommends content by mood. Personal Intelligence connects Gmail and Calendar. US rollout.

Disney is testing AI-powered search inside both ESPN and Disney+, the company announced on Wednesday. ESPN Search lets a small group of users ask sports questions in natural language and receive answers, stats, related content, and recommendations drawn from decades of ESPN’s articles, videos, research data, and internal knowledge repositories. On Disney+, a separate beta lets subscribers describe what they want to watch in their own words, moving from “I don’t know what to watch” to recommendations based on immediate mood rather than viewing history alone.

The Disney+ tool accepts natural language, voice input, or suggested prompts. A subscriber who normally watches crime dramas but wants something lighthearted can say so, and the system surfaces content that fits the moment rather than the pattern. ESPN Search works similarly: a fan can ask a question like “who has the most rushing yards in a single playoff game” and get an answer with supporting content rather than a list of links. Both features are in limited beta in the US with no announced launch date.

The more notable addition is Personal Intelligence, which lets the AI pull context from a user’s Gmail and Google Calendar to personalise answers. A subscriber with a flight to Vancouver in their inbox can ask what time they land and get an answer without leaving the app. It is off by default. The feature also remembers prior conversations, so trip planning can be resumed without starting over. Amazon is rebuilding Prime Video around AI recommendations in a project called Lighthouse, and Netflix is using generative AI to solve the content overload its own catalogue created. Disney is now entering the same race.

The competitive pressure is real. Every major streaming platform is chasing the same problem: viewers spend too long deciding what to watch and sometimes give up entirely. AI search that understands mood, context, and intent is the bet all three companies are now making. Disney’s version is the earliest stage of the three, a beta with a small group and no scale figures. Whether it reaches all subscribers depends on what the tests show. For now, the streaming wars have a new front: who can help you decide fastest.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Disney+ 和 ESPN 正在小规模用户群体中测试人工智能搜索。 ESPN 回答自然语言体育问题。 Disney+ 根据心情推荐内容。 个人智能连接 Gmail 和日历。 美国推出。

迪士尼周三宣布，正在 ESPN 和 Disney+ 内测试人工智能驱动的搜索。 ESPN 搜索允许一小群用户用自然语言提出体育问题，并接收来自 ESPN 数十年文章、视频、研究数据和内部知识库的答案、统计数据、相关内容和推荐。 在 Disney+ 上，一个单独的测试版允许订阅者用自己的话描述他们想看什么，从“我不知道该看什么”转变为基于即时情绪的推荐，而不是仅仅观看历史。

Disney+ 工具接受自然语言、语音输入或建议提示。 通常观看犯罪剧但想要一些轻松的内容的订阅者可以这样说，系统会显示适合当下而不是模式的内容。 ESPN 搜索的工作原理类似：球迷可以提出诸如“一场季后赛中谁冲球码数最多”之类的问题，并通过支持内容而不是链接列表获得答案。 这两项功能在美国均处于有限测试阶段，尚未公布发布日期。

更值得注意的新增功能是个人智能，它可以让人工智能从用户的 Gmail 和 Google 日历中提取上下文来个性化答案。 收件箱中有飞往温哥华航班的订户可以询问航班降落时间，无需离开应用程序即可获得答案。 默认情况下它是关闭的。 该功能还可以记住之前的对话，因此无需重新开始即可恢复旅行计划。 亚马逊正在一个名为 Lighthouse 的项目中围绕人工智能推荐重建 Prime Video，而 Netflix 正在使用生成式人工智能来解决其自己创建的目录内容过载问题。 迪士尼现在也加入了同样的竞赛。

竞争压力是真实存在的。 每个主要的流媒体平台都面临着同样的问题：观众花费太长时间来决定观看什么，有时甚至完全放弃。 理解情绪、情境和意图的人工智能搜索是这三家公司目前所下的赌注。 迪士尼版本是这三个版本中最早的一个，是一个小规模的测试版，没有比例人物。 它是否到达所有订阅者取决于测试结果。 目前，流媒体战争有了新的战线：谁能帮助你最快做出决定。
